dockerEdit.title: Edit the container {name}
dockerEdit.tabs.label: Container settings sections
dockerEdit.f.name: Name
dockerEdit.hint.cmd: Empty: the command from the image. Arguments are separated by spaces, quotes are supported.
dockerEdit.hint.retries: 0: no limit on the number of retries.
dockerEdit.hint.mem: Using {used} now. Below that the container is killed for lack of memory.
dockerEdit.hint.memIdle: Empty or 0: no limit. At least 6 MB.
dockerEdit.hint.cpus: 0.5 means half of one core. Empty or 0: no limit.
dockerEdit.notice.composeMain: Compose project {project}: the name, the image and the command are set in the compose file. The restart policy and the limits can be changed on the spot, but the next update of the project brings back the values from the file.
dockerEdit.notice.composeOther: The container belongs to the compose project {project}. These settings come from the file {file}: a change made around it is lost at the next update of the project. The file can be opened in the Files tab.
dockerEdit.port.empty: No ports are published. The container is reachable only from its own docker networks.
dockerEdit.port.hint: The address 127.0.0.1 opens the port to the server itself, 0.0.0.0 to the whole network. Docker bypasses the server firewall: check the Firewall tab.
dockerEdit.mount.empty: No volumes. The container's data lives only inside it and is lost when it is deleted.
dockerEdit.mount.hint: Volumes left alone move to the new container as they are, the data is neither copied nor lost.
dockerEdit.env.hint: The values of passwords, tokens and keys are hidden. Only the variable names go into the audit log.
dockerEdit.foot.discardText: There are unsaved changes ({n}). Close without applying?
dockerEdit.review.warn: The container {name} will be stopped for a few seconds. The data in volumes is kept, the data inside the container itself (outside volumes) is lost.
dockerEdit.review.step1: The image is pulled if it was changed.
dockerEdit.review.step2: The container is stopped and renamed to {name}-linager-old-….
dockerEdit.review.step3: A new container is created and started with the same networks and volumes.
dockerEdit.review.step4: If it does not stay running, the previous one comes back. If all is well, the old one is deleted.
dockerEdit.review.stepsLive: The changes are applied on the spot, the container keeps running.
dockerEdit.diff.name: Name
dockerEdit.err.name: Name: letters, digits, "_", "." and "-", not starting with a sign.
dockerEdit.err.image: Enter an image name, for example nginx:1.26-alpine.
dockerEdit.err.cmd: A quote in the command is not closed.
dockerEdit.err.hostPort: Host port: a number from 1 to 65535.
dockerEdit.err.contPort: Container port: a number from 1 to 65535.
dockerEdit.err.portBusy: Port {port} is already used by the container {name}.
dockerEdit.err.bindSrc: The path on the server must be absolute: /srv/data.
dockerEdit.err.dst: The path in the container must be absolute.
dockerEdit.err.dstDup: The path {path} is already used by another volume.
dockerEdit.err.envName: Variable name: Latin letters, digits and "_", not starting with a digit.
dockerEdit.err.mem: Memory: a whole number of MB, at least 6.
dockerEdit.err.cpus: CPU: a number above 0 and at most 128.
console.soon: The Console (terminals, desktops and the assistant of several servers) comes in a later stage. The chosen section is remembered.
usr.loadFailed: Could not get the list of users
usr.legend: Showing {shown} of {total}. Orange groups (sudo, docker) give almost full access to the server. The tab counts as "root access": an operator sees it only if the administrator gave them the Users module.
usr.sudo.pwHint: sudo asks for the password of the user
usr.sudo.nopwHint: NOPASSWD: ALL, dangerous: anyone who signs in as this user becomes root
usr.confirm.lock.title: Lock "{user}"?
usr.confirm.lock.text: {user} will not be able to sign in with a password or a key. Their sessions will be ended.
usr.confirm.lock.hint: The lock can be removed at any time. The processes of the session stop with it.
usr.confirm.unlock.title: Unlock "{user}"?
usr.confirm.unlock.text: {user} will be able to sign in again.
usr.confirm.unlock.hint: The password and the keys stay as they were.
usr.confirm.kill.title: End the sessions of "{user}"?
usr.confirm.kill.text: All sessions of {user} ({n} now) will be ended together with their processes.
usr.confirm.kill.hint: This is not a lock: the user can sign in again.
usr.props.title: Properties: {user}
usr.props.system: This is a system account: the panel does not change it.
usr.props.lastAdmin: This is the only unlocked user with sudo and root cannot log in. Give sudo to another user first.
usr.props.lockHint: the password and the key stop working, the sessions are ended
usr.props.audit: Changes are applied on the server at once, each one is written to the audit log.
usr.add.title: Add user

usr.add.taken: A user with this name already exists
usr.pw.generateHint: 20 characters, a random password made in the browser
usr.pw.once: Copy the password now: it cannot be seen again after it is set.
usr.pw.title: New password for {user}
usr.del.title: Delete "{user}"?
usr.del.irreversible: This cannot be undone. The account disappears from the server.
usr.del.running: The user has {s} sessions and {p} processes now. They will be ended.
usr.del.homeHint: otherwise the files stay on disk without an owner
usr.del.keys: SSH keys in their directory: {n}. They are lost when the directory is deleted.

common.genericError: Something went wrong, please try again
sec.noSsh: No SSH server was found on this host.
sec.noLog: The SSH login log is not available (no journald and no /var/log/auth.log).
sec.shortLog: The log keeps records only since {date}: the data does not cover all days.
sec.shortLogUnknown: Could not tell how far back the log goes: the data may be incomplete.
sec.truncated: The log is very large: only a part of it was read, the numbers are approximate.
sec.hint.root: Allow root only by key or forbid it
sec.hint.password: Better turn it off and keep key login only
sec.hint.pubkey: Turn key login on and add your key, so you do not depend on passwords
sec.hint.empty: Forbid empty passwords at once (PermitEmptyPasswords no)
sec.hint.allow: Limit who may log in with AllowUsers or AllowGroups
sec.hint.f2b: Install or start fail2ban to ban brute-force attempts
sec.hint.auto: Turn on unattended-upgrades so security fixes arrive by themselves
sec.hint.secupd: Install them on the Updates tab
sec.hint.reboot: Reboot the server at a convenient time to apply the updates
sec.allow.no: not set, any user may log in
sec.failures.sub: from {addresses} addresses; probes of users that do not exist: {invalid}
sec.failures.none: There were no failed attempts in the period.
sec.badge.prior: {n} failed attempts from this address before
sec.badge.priorHint: This address guessed passwords earlier and then logged in. Worth checking.
sec.logins.none: There were no successful logins in the period.
sec.keys.hint: The authorized_keys of every user with a shell. Only fingerprints are shown, the keys themselves are not sent.
sec.end.confirm: End the session of {user} from {ip}? All its processes will be stopped, including those the user started (tmux, screen, long operations).
sec.end.confirmUser: End all SSH sessions of {user} ({n})? Their processes will be stopped, including those the user started (tmux, screen, long operations).
sec.end.hint: This is not a block: the user can sign in again if they have a password or a key. To close the access, change the password or remove the key.
sec.f2b.failuresWeek: failed sign-in attempts in a week
sec.f2b.why: fail2ban watches the SSH log and blocks addresses that guess passwords. That removes most of the noise and the load.
sec.f2b.selfNote: Your address {ip} and the network 127.0.0.0/8 are never blocked.
sec.f2b.laterNote: The threshold can be changed later.
sec.f2b.installText: The package will be installed and SSH protection switched on with the threshold "{preset}":
sec.f2b.installNote: The action is written to the audit log. If the package manager is busy, the agent waits up to two minutes.
sec.f2b.installed: fail2ban is installed and protects SSH
sec.f2b.noSshd: SSH protection (the sshd jail) is off. Open the settings and save them to switch it on.
sec.f2b.manual.self: The panel will not block your own address.
sec.f2b.summaryLong: An address is blocked after {n} failed sign-in attempts within {min} min, for {ban}.
sec.f2b.orManual: or set the values by hand
sec.f2b.increment: Lengthen the ban at every repeat (twice, at most 7 days)
sec.f2b.recidive: Block for 7 days the addresses that were banned 3 times in a day (recidive)
sec.f2b.ignore.placeholder: an address or a network, for example 203.0.113.0/24
sec.f2b.ignore.bad: This is not an address or a network.
sec.f2b.ignore.note: Your current address always stays in the exceptions.
sec.f2b.saveNote: fail2ban rereads its settings and the current bans stay. The change is written to the audit log.
sec.f2b.bans.audit: Bans and unbans are written to the audit log.
sec.f2b.unbanAllText: Unban all addresses ({n})? They can guess passwords again until fail2ban blocks them anew.
sec.f2b.hist.error: The log {path} is not available: the history appears once fail2ban writes to it.
sec.f2b.hist.shown: The last {n} of {total} events of the log {path}
sec.keys.removeText: Remove the key {fp} of {user} from authorized_keys?
sec.keys.removeNote: A copy of the file (authorized_keys.bak-DATE) is saved next to it first. Sessions that are already open stay. The action is written to the audit log.
sec.keys.warnLast: This is the last key of {user}. Without it key sign-in will not work.
sec.keys.warnLockout: This is the last key of {user} and password sign-in is off: after removing it nobody can sign in over SSH as this user.

net.config.confirmText: The changed interfaces will be brought up again with the new configuration. If the connection to the server is lost and you do not confirm the change within 30 seconds, the agent restores the previous file by itself.
net.config.hintNetplan: One file from /etc/netplan is edited. Files are read in alphabetical order and merged, a later file overrides an earlier one, so check the "Effective configuration". The file is checked with netplan generate and applied with a 30-second rollback.
net.config.fileInvalid: Name: Latin letters, digits, . _ -, ending in .yaml.
net.config.cloudInit: This file is generated by cloud-init and may be overwritten on reboot. To keep your edits, disable cloud-init network management (file /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d/99-disable-network-config.cfg with the line network: {config: disabled}) or create your own file with a later name.
net.dns.edit.title: Edit DNS
net.dns.edit.searchHint: up to 6, separated by spaces or commas
net.dns.edit.note: The change starts a confirmation window: if you do not confirm, the agent restores the previous DNS settings by itself.

net.dns.err.domain: One of the domains is not a valid host name

fw.ufwWarning: ufw is active on the server: ufw and nftables rules may conflict
fw.loadError: Could not load the firewall. Retrying automatically.
fw.status.active: Rules are active · /etc/nftables.conf · changes are applied with a rollback in 30 s.
fw.chain.empty: No rules. The chain policy applies.
fw.add.title: Add rule
fw.add.rawToggle: Enter a rule in nft syntax
fw.add.errPortProto: A port can only be set for tcp and udp.
fw.add.errPortFormat: Port: a number or a comma-separated list, for example 80,443.
fw.add.errPortRange: The port must be between 1 and 65535.
fw.add.errSource: Source: an address or a network, for example 10.0.0.0/8.
fw.add.errEmpty: A rule without conditions matches all packets. Add a port, a source or a comment.
fw.draft.title: There are unapplied changes
fw.draft.hint: Nothing changes on the server until you press Apply.
fw.warn.title: Apply rules with risk?
fw.warn.explain: The server warns about possible consequences. If the agent connection is lost, the rules cannot be confirmed and the server will roll them back by itself.
fw.pending.title: Confirm the rules
fw.pending.explain: The rules are active on the server. Confirm them before the countdown ends. Unconfirmed rules are rolled back automatically by the server.
fw.pending.expired: Time is up, the rules are being rolled back…
fw.pending.lost: Connection to the server is lost. If the rules are not confirmed, the server will roll them back by itself.
fw.ruleset.title: nft list ruleset
fw.otherTables: Other tables: {tables}. They are managed by other programs, for example Docker, and are not edited here.
fw.add.errList: The address list does not exist. Create it in the "Address lists" window.
fw.sets.title: Address lists
fw.sets.help: Named lists of addresses and networks. Use one in the Source field of a rule as @name, for example @office. An address is added to a list once and any number of rules can use it.
fw.sets.errName: Name: lowercase latin letters, digits and _, starts with a letter, up to 31 characters.
fw.sets.errExists: A list with this name already exists.
fw.sets.deleteBlocked: The list is used in rules. Remove those rules first.
fw.sets.errAddr: Not an address of this family: {items}
fw.sets.draftNote: Changes go to the firewall draft and take effect after applying, with a rollback in 30 seconds.
fw.sets.pickOrCreate: Pick a list on the left or create a new one.
fw.ports.title: Ports and connections
fw.ports.error: Could not get the list of ports.
fw.ports.noSs: The ss command is missing on the server, the list of ports is unavailable.
fw.ports.exposed: Reachable from outside without a firewall rule: {n}.
fw.ports.plan: Port {port} is open to everyone: {process} listens on it and no rule covers it.
fw.ports.modeRestrict: Allow only from a network or a list
fw.ports.needSource: Enter a network, an address or an address list.
fw.ports.planNote: The rule goes to the firewall draft, at the end of the input chain. Applying needs a confirmation and rolls back after 30 seconds, as always.
fw.ports.noRemotes: There are no incoming connections right now.
fw.ports.how: "Allowed by a rule" means the input chain has an explicit rule for the port. "No rule" means the process listens on all interfaces and the firewall lets the traffic through by the chain policy. 127.0.0.1 is not visible from outside. Ports published by Docker go through the forward chain and are not controlled by input rules.
fw.chain.established: Replies of connections that already exist (established,related) are always allowed: the rule is added automatically first in every chain and is not shown in the list.
fw.add.systemRule: This rule is added to every chain automatically, there is no need to add it.
fw.log.toggle: Write the matches of this rule to the journal
fw.log.title: Firewall journal
fw.log.unavailable: journalctl is missing on the server, the journal of matches is unavailable.
fw.log.howto: The journal shows which packets matched which rules. The firewall writes nothing by itself: switch the record on for the rules you care about.
fw.log.step1: Switch the record on for the rules below. A log statement with a mark is added to the rule.
fw.log.step2: Apply the rules as usual: a confirmation and a rollback in 30 seconds.
fw.log.step3: The matches appear here in a few seconds. They are kept for 7 days.
fw.log.limitNote: The record of a busy rule grows fast: such rules are limited to 5 records per second.
fw.log.enableDrops: Switch on for all drop rules
fw.log.applyNote: The switches change the draft. Close the window and apply the draft on the firewall tab.
fw.log.groupHint: Identical events (chain, action, protocol, source, port) merge into one row with a counter
fw.log.truncated: only the newest records are shown
fw.log.source: The records come from the kernel journal (the lg: mark), so the history survives a restart of the agent.
fw.log.noList: The address list does not exist.
fw.log.wrongFamily: The address is of another family than the list @{list}.
fw.log.addedToList: {ip} is added to the draft of the list @{list}. Apply the draft on the firewall tab.
fw.log.blocked: A rule for {ip} is added first in input. Apply the draft on the firewall tab.
fw.log.markedNote: The rules are marked. Apply the draft on the firewall tab: the matches appear here as soon as matching traffic passes.
docker.update.title: Update the container {name}
docker.update.text: The image is pulled again and the container is recreated with the same settings. It stops for a moment; if the new one does not start, the old one is brought back.
docker.update.compose: The container was created by docker compose: the service of the project is updated with docker compose pull and up -d.
pult.placeholder: Pick a server on the left
pult.placeholderSub: The session opens here, the tabs open above.
pult.loadFailed: Could not load the list of servers.
assist.name: Assistant
assist.offline: The server is offline: the Assistant is not available.
assist.connectingHint: The agent starts the helper in the session; waiting for the first frame.
assist.wakingHint: The screen of the computer is off; switching it on. It takes a few seconds.
assist.limit: This session is already open in another Assistant window. Close that window or pick another session.
assist.lost: The connection was lost. Check that the server is online and connect again.
manage.lead: How the Assistant connects to this computer, and the Windows remote desktop. Changes apply at once, to the open sessions too.
manage.auto: Lower the quality and the frame rate by itself when the limit is not met
manage.estimate: Estimate while working actively: up to {peak} Mbit/s, about {idle} Mbit/s at rest (the picture does not change, no frames are sent).
manage.saved: Saved · applied to the open sessions: {n}
manage.rdpHome: This edition of Windows ({edition}) cannot host a remote desktop: it has no RDP service. The Assistant works without RDP and is not affected.
manage.rdpOnNote: The RDP tab works through the Windows Remote Desktop service. If you turn it off, the tab offers to turn it on again.
manage.rdpOffNote: While the remote desktop is off the RDP tab is not available. The Assistant keeps working.
manage.rdpOffText: Windows will stop accepting RDP connections: signing in by remote desktop is forbidden on the computer and the firewall rule "Remote Desktop" is turned off. Sessions that are open now stay, new ones cannot connect.
manage.rdpOffNote2: The agent and the Assistant do not depend on RDP and keep working. The action is written to the audit log.
manage.noSessions: Nobody is signed in to Windows now.
manage.noModule: The agent of this computer cannot list sessions: update it.
assist.clipTooBig: The text in the clipboard is too long: at most 1 MB can be sent.
assist.clipDenied: The browser did not give access to the clipboard. Allow it for this page and try again.
assist.clipEmpty: The clipboard of the computer is empty
manage.cursorShow: Show the remote computer's pointer in the picture
manage.cursorHint: Unchecked, the pointer is not in the picture: only your own pointer is shown, and it moves without delay.
manage.sasNote: For the Ctrl+Alt+Del button of the Assistant to work, Windows must allow services to send the secure attention sequence. This changes the Windows policy "Software SAS generation". The button works in the console session only.
manage.sasAllowText: The Windows policy "Software SAS generation" will change on the computer: services will be able to send Ctrl+Alt+Del. This lets the Assistant bring up the security screen in the console session.
manage.sasDenyText: The Windows policy "Software SAS generation" will change on the computer: services will not be allowed to send Ctrl+Alt+Del. The Ctrl+Alt+Del button of the Assistant will stop working.
manage.sasNote2: This is a Windows security setting. The action is written to the audit log.
manage.sasAllowed: Ctrl+Alt+Del from the Assistant is allowed
manage.sasDenied: Ctrl+Alt+Del from the Assistant is forbidden
assist.typeDesktop: Typing refused: the screen is not a sign-in or a UAC prompt now.
assist.typeUnsupported: This computer cannot type on the sign-in screen.
desk.title: Remote desktop
desk.note: The password travels only inside the protected connection and is never stored. Only the login is remembered. The connection is written to the audit log.
desk.offline: The server is offline: the desktop is not available.
desk.off: Remote desktop is turned off in Windows.
desk.notListening: The Remote Desktop service does not answer.
desk.unsupported: This edition of Windows ({edition}) cannot host a remote desktop.
desk.err.denied: Access denied: this account may not sign in over remote desktop.
desk.err.proxy: Could not reach the desktop through the agent. Check that the service is on and the agent is online.
desk.err.negotiation: The Windows server refused the security negotiation (TLS or network level authentication is required).
desk.cadHint: Send Ctrl+Alt+Del to the remote computer
desk.clipDenied: The browser did not allow access to the clipboard: allow it for this page (HTTPS is needed).
keys.title: Keys
keys.intro: Keys is your personal encrypted file of logins and passwords. You keep it, it is not on the server, and it fills the RDP form. The panel decrypts it in the memory of this tab only: after the tab is closed or the page is reloaded, open the file again.
keys.create.title: Create a vault
keys.create.warn: The passphrase cannot be recovered: if you forget it, the file cannot be opened. Keep the file in a safe place and make a copy.
keys.create.hint: At least {n} characters; a phrase of several words is better.
keys.created: The file {name} is created. Keep it in a safe place: the phrase cannot be recovered.
keys.open.title: Open a file
keys.err.auth: Wrong passphrase, or the file was changed.
keys.err.format: This is not a Keys vault file.
keys.err.version: The file was made by a newer version of the panel.
keys.err.limit: The file or the vault is too large.
keys.lock.label: Lock after
keys.lock.waiting: The lock time is over. Save the file and the vault closes.
keys.closeAsk.title: Close without saving?
keys.closeAsk.text: The changes that are not in the file will be lost.
keys.col.name: Name
keys.empty: There are no keys in the vault yet. "Add a key" makes the first one.
keys.legend: Passwords are not shown in the table: they are only in the window of a key. "Close the window" leaves the vault open until the tab is closed; "Close the vault" forgets the decrypted data at once. A binding only sets the order in the lists: every key of the file is open to whoever opened it.
keys.bind.goneTitle: Part of the binding points to a server or a group that is not in the panel any more
